text: Article · research post · Q Labs Research (qlabs.sh) Dust: Pretraining Transformers Without Backpropagation Samip Dahal, Bishwas Mandal, Serdar Gülbahar, Akshay Vegesna (Q Labs) · published 5 October 2026 In one line: A research post with code: Dust adds independent noise to each layer's activations at every token, credits each token's noise with that token's own loss change, and forms the weight update as backprop does (estimated error times input); on a 37.7M-parameter GPT trained with constant-rate SGD (three seeds per cell), 16,384 draws per update end slightly below backprop at 100k and 1M tokens (6 and 61 updates) and 0.06 and 0.17 above it at 10M and 20M, at about 5,000 times backprop's compute per update by our count, while the authors' weight-space ES baseline would need an extrapolated 3,000 to 23,000 times the population to match Dust's smallest setting.

text: The evidence, judged . read it (20 min) · logs and code (qlabs-eng/dust, MIT) · discussion (280 points, 82 comments on 27 November 2026) The idea in one sentence: add independent noise to a layer's outputs at every token , score each token's noise by the change in that token's loss, and average over many noisy forward passes: this estimates the error backprop would deliver to the layer, the update is formed as backprop forms it (error times input), and since every token is a separate trial, one pass runs thousands of trials where weight-space evolution strategies run one.
label: core

text: Token t's reward is its centred loss reduction c t (the mean perturbed loss there across draws, minus this draw's), plus, with a decay γ, the reductions at later tokens its jitter reaches through attention: r t = Σ s≥t γ s−t c s , ĝ t = −(1/Kσ) Σ i r t (i) a t (i) , Ĝ W = Σ t ĝ t x t ⊤ The middle term is the idea: the reward-weighted noise, averaged over K draws, points along the error at the layer's output (Equations 1 to 3); it is REINFORCE for a Gaussian policy with a baseline ( Policy gradients and actor-critic ).
